items.author: Aaron Levie
items.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
items.summary_en:
The average strongly held belief these days in AI has a half life of 6 months at best. Here are just a few the industry has cycled through and probably has no consensus on at the moment:

* OSS is too far behind to catch up 

* The labs can’t be profitable at scale

* All software will be replaced by agents

* You can’t build moats on top of models

* Cheaper models will mean less compute

* You don’t need evals

* RAG is dead 

* AI will decimate engineering jobs

* Prompting won’t matter in the future 

* We’ve hit a training wall

* Frontier models are too dangerous to release 

…and dozens and dozens more. The key here is to remain flexible in your thinking because we’re going to be in a constant state of change for a while.
items.summary_zh:
AI 圈那些被说得斩钉截铁的信念，半衰期最多 6 个月：开源追不上、Agent 会替代所有软件、RAG 已死、工程师要被干掉、训练撞墙……一轮轮被推翻又重来。

真正该坚持的不是某个判断，而是在持续剧变里保持脑子可变形。

items.author: Madhu Guru
items.bio: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
items.summary_en:
AI product building has a ~3-month playbook half-life. Here’s how to adapt.

Most trad product teams are built to discover a playbook and then milk it for the next 5 years.

However in the AI labs, we consciously throw away playbooks every few months cos we start seeing diminishing returns.

Here’s what you can do as an AI builder:

Focus on defining a set of meta-principles for 
1/ how you continuously learn what the market wants today and what it might want in 3 months
2/ how you execute with extreme urgency

The specifics of 1 and 2 will vary based on your domain and product type.
Build a team that learns and adapts at that pace. 

Legacy teams are optimized for playbook milking.

AI teams need to be optimized for inventing.
items.summary_zh: AI 产品打法的半衰期只有 3 个月，传统团队那套“找到剧本吃 5 年”的模式已经失效。AI builder 真正要优化的不是复用 playbook，而是持续判断市场变化、极速执行，并组建一支能不断重造打法的团队。

items.author: Thibault Sottiaux
items.bio: Codex & ChatGPT @OpenAI
items.summary_en:
We unfortunately have decided that we cannot continue providing access to our models through Cursor and are ending our partnership. It boils down to trust and we’ve asked that this takes effect on November 12 to give you some time to plan.

Many have used the GPT models through Cursor and here are options we know should work in the future:

- We will continue to allow using your own OpenAI API key and similarly will continue to provide access through our IDE extensions for Cursor.
- We will keep working with the broadest range of tools and harnesses, some of which are OSS, but also many many closed-source ones.

We are as committed as ever to continue supporting developers and the flourishing ecosystem of tools, harnesses and products. We will also continue to invest in our own open-source initiatives and believe in broad optionality for developers.

You can read more about our decision in the blog:
https://t.co/Oj76Bkc2KX
items.summary_zh: OpenAI 和 Cursor 分手，核心原因说白了就是“不再信任”，模型接入会在 11 月 12 日结束。以后还能用自己的 OpenAI API Key 或 IDE 扩展，但 Cursor 这条官方合作通道没了。

items.author: Guillermo Rauch
items.bio: @vercel CEO
items.summary_en:
I see the web evolving in two extremes:

1️⃣ ultra-fancy human experiences, in the service of delight, exploration, brand, entertainment. https://t.co/0nyTRPKDEJ / threejs / typegpu are enabling this

2️⃣ agent-centric content, data and APIs. the opposite end of the spectrum: pure, lossless signal for machines. The rise of markdown and MCP are the tip of this iceberg

The 'in between' is likely to be subsumed by agents producing just-in-time UI. When you need utilitarian content or data, it'll be generated just-in-time for you. Think of the agent as the new browser in this model.
items.summary_zh:
Web 会分裂成两个极端：一端是为人类打造的炫技体验，服务愉悦、探索、品牌和娱乐；另一端是面向 Agent 的内容、数据和 API，只追求给机器的无损信号。

中间层会被 Agent 吞掉：实用型内容和数据不再需要固定页面，而是由 Agent 即时生成 UI，Agent 就是新的浏览器。

items.summary_en:
It's interesting to me to see a lot of people comment on visa stuff without actually going through it.

I am a proud American citizen who has also had the following visas: F1, OPT, CPT, H1-B, EB-3 Green Card etc.

I think ALL of the following things can be true:
1/ There is abuse of the H1-B system. We should 100% stop that. It prevents legitimate use cases. I am glad the government is doing something about this.

2/ We make it too hard for truly high-skilled workers to stay in the USA. It is a huge source of strength for us that the sharpest minds in the world WANT to come here. 

3/ In particular, high-skilled Indians have it harder than most. 

4/ In any country, the laws and regulations should prioritize it's own citizens.
items.summary_zh:
很多没真正走过签证流程的人在对 H1-B 指点江山；这个系统确实有滥用，必须砍掉，但美国也把真正高技能人才留下来搞得太难了。

美国的强大之一在于全世界最聪明的人愿意来，尤其高技能印度人承受了不成比例的难度；同时，任何国家的法律都该优先照顾本国公民。

My hot take is that Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work are partial solutions and that Grok Bot is the right end state for a capable AI agent product for non-technical people.

Grok Bot I think people can easily "grok" that it's a computer that runs in the cloud. 

If you asked people to explain what the difference between ChatGPT Work and Codex is (e.g., Work can run cloud tasks but Codex cannot) or how Claude Cowork actually works I bet most people have no idea.

items.author: No Priors
items.title: Rethinking Legacy Data Infrastructure with Eon Co-Founders Ofir Ehrlich and Gonen Stein
items.summary_en:
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:22
Up until now, the concerns came from human threats. What we're seeing now on steroids is that the same type of threat is coming from nonhuman actors, agents that essentially have legitimate access to the environment with legitimate permissions. Fortunately for us, it's a very similar methodology in terms of detecting that and protecting against that, but the velocity of that happening is extreme.

Speaker 2 | 00:22 - 00:51
Think of the nontechnical people. They're not even aware for things like security or compliance or who is gonna use this data. Maybe their agent that they are building are using other agents, and they're not technical to even understand what it means. It creates complete set of actors inside the organization, not bound by the rules of the organization and not necessarily running within the premises of the organization, but handling sensitive data. It's a good thing and bad thing that everyone inside the organization can become builders.

Speaker 2 | 00:51 - 00:52
We live in very interesting times.

Speaker 3 | 00:59 - 01:25
Today on our priors, we're joined by Ofer Oerlech and Goenen Stein, the cofounders of EON. EON is a cloud backup disaster recovery centric services designed for the AI era. In this discussion, we talk about data, AI, why Google bought out the data of Spirit Airlines out of bankruptcy, and what it means to really manage and use data infrastructure in the AI era. Ophelia Gunnen, thank you so much for joining me Enterprise today. It's great to see you.

Speaker 1 | 01:25 - 01:27
Absolutely. Thanks for having us.

Speaker 3 | 01:27 - 01:49
Yeah. So one thing that you guys are doing at EON is or, why don't you give a quick overview of EON and what it does really quickly? Because I think that'll set the context
items.summary_zh: AI 代理正在把安全威胁从“人类黑客”升级成拥有合法权限、速度极快的内部行动者，传统规则和边界被彻底打穿。人人都能成为 builder 是机会，也是风险：非技术员工可能在不理解安全、合规和数据责任的情况下，让一整套不受组织约束的代理处理敏感数据。
